title: Claude Code as a Daily Driver: Claude.md, Skills, Subagents, Plugins, and MCPs
description: A deep dive into using Claude Code as a daily driver, covering Claude.md files, Skills, Subagents, Plugins, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations. This comprehensive guide explores advanced workflows for AI-assisted development.
author: arps18

title: I'm Tired of Talking to AI
description: A personal reflection on AI fatigue and the changing nature of human-computer interaction as AI assistants become more prevalent in daily workflows.
author: theorchid

title: Cognition raises $1B at $25B pre-money valuation
description: AI coding startup Cognition has raised $1 billion in funding at a $25 billion pre-money valuation, highlighting the massive investment flowing into AI development tools.
author: Julie Bort

title: Security Center 2.0: Act on vulnerabilities in bulk across all your apps
description: Replit announced Security Center 2.0, making it easier to understand security posture across all Replit projects and remediate urgent security holes across multiple published projects in seconds. The system breaks down exposure by critical and high severity vulnerabilities.
author: Replit

title: Secure more apps with External Access Tokens and Private Publishing
description: Replit expanded secure access for builders with Private Publishing now available to Core and Starter plan users, and External Access Tokens for all private apps. Private Publishing works at the network level to prevent unauthorized requests.
author: Replit

title: MUSE-Autoskill: Self-Evolving Agents via Skill Creation, Memory, Management, and Evaluation
description: Researchers from Huawei and others propose MUSE-Autoskill, a framework for self-evolving AI agents that can create, manage, and evaluate their own skills, enabling continuous improvement through skill acquisition and refinement.
author: Huawei Lin, Peng Li, et al.

title: Natural Language Query to Configuration for Retrieval Agents
description: Researchers from Stanford and Databricks propose a system for converting natural language queries into configurations for retrieval agents, making it easier to customize agent behavior without deep technical knowledge.
author: Melissa Z. Pan, Negar Arabzadeh, et al.

title: Alignment Tampering: How RLHF Is Exploited to Optimize Misaligned Biases
description: ICML 2026 paper exploring how reinforcement learning from human feedback can be exploited to optimize misaligned biases, revealing potential vulnerabilities in current alignment techniques.
author: Dongyoon Hahm, Dylan Hadfield-Menell, Kimin Lee

title: Maat: The Agentic Legal Research Assistant for Competition Protection
description: Researchers from Egypt introduce Maat, an AI agent designed to assist with legal research in the domain of competition protection, demonstrating how AI agents can be specialized for complex legal domains.
author: Basant Mounir, Farida Madkour, et al.

title: Modeling Agentic Technical Debt and Stochastic Tax
description: A framework for measuring, simulating, and dashboarding the technical debt and 'stochastic tax' incurred by AI agents, providing tools to understand the long-term costs of agentic systems.
author: Muhammad Zia Hydari, Raja Iqbal, Narayan Ramasubbu

title: SIA: Self Improving AI with Harness & Weight Updates
description: Researchers propose SIA, a self-improving AI system that uses harness mechanisms and weight updates to continuously enhance its capabilities, exploring methods for autonomous AI improvement.
author: Prannay Hebbar, Yogendra Manawat, et al.

title: The pressure - AI-assisted security reports overwhelming curl team
description: Daniel Stenberg reports that the curl team is facing unprecedented pressure with 4-5x more security reports than in 2024, averaging more than one report per day. The quality is higher than ever, with very detailed reports, but the workload is immense. Most vulnerabilities found have been LOW or MEDIUM severity, with the most recent HIGH severity CVE in October 2023.
author: Daniel Stenberg (via Simon Willison)

title: Microsoft Copilot Cowork Exfiltrates Files
description: Microsoft Copilot Cowork allowed agents to send emails to the user's inbox without approval, but those messages could leak data to attackers via rendered images. Because messages can contain external images that trigger network requests, data can be exfiltrated when a user opens a compromised message. OneDrive can create pre-authenticated download links that could be leaked via prompt injection.
author: Simon Willison

title: Paul Graham on AI-written emails from founders
description: Paul Graham criticizes the trend of founders using AI to write emails in a hard-hitting journalistic style, noting he has never finished reading an email signed by a human but written by AI. He describes it as feeling like being lied to, making him think less of the author who can't write well unaided and are trying to trick him.
author: Paul Graham (via Simon Willison)

title: Notes on Pope Leo XIV's encyclical on AI
description: The Vatican released 'Magnifica Humanitas' by Pope Leo XIV on safeguarding the human person in the time of artificial intelligence. Simon describes it as some of the clearest writing he's seen on the ethics of integrating AI into modern society.
author: Simon Willison

title: Armin Ronacher on AI-generated GitHub issues
description: Armin Ronacher expresses frustration with people submitting issues not in their own voice - problems thrown into an LLM that reworded them into messes of inaccurate conclusions, fake-minimal repros, and wrong implementation strategies. He prefers issue reports condensed to what the human actually observed: the command run, expected behavior, what happened instead, and exact error/logs.
author: Armin Ronacher (via Simon Willison)

title: FTC Settles Charges Over Deceptive 'Active Listening' AI Marketing
description: FTC requires Cox Media Group and two other firms to pay nearly $1 million to settle charges they deceived customers about an 'Active Listening' AI-powered marketing service. The companies claimed to listen to consumer conversations through smart devices, but actually just resold email lists from other data brokers at a markup. FTC clarified that clicking through terms of service doesn't constitute adequate consent for invasive data collection.
author: Simon Willison

title: The memory shortage is causing a repricing of consumer electronics
description: David Oks explains why consumer products using memory will get more expensive. Memory manufacturers (only three large companies remain) have fixed wafer capacity split between DDR, LPDDR, and HBM. HBM for GPUs grew from 2% to expected 20% of wafer allocation by end of 2026, and HBM consumes more than 3x the wafer capacity per GB than DDR or LPDDR. This already impacts sub-$100 smartphones important to African and South Asian markets.
author: David Oks (via Simon Willison)

title: Datasette Agent - extensible AI assistant for Datasette
description: Simon announced the first release of Datasette Agent, a new extensible AI assistant for Datasette. After working on his LLM Python library for just over three years, this represents the moment LLM and Datasette finally come together.
author: Simon Willison

title: SpaceX S-1: Anthropic paying $1.25B/month for compute capacity
description: SpaceX filing reveals Cloud Services Agreements with Anthropic for access to compute capacity across COLOSSUS and COLOSSUS II. Anthropic agreed to pay $1.25 billion per month through May 2029, with capacity ramping in May-June 2026 at reduced fee. Agreements terminable by either party upon 90 days notice.
author: Simon Willison

title: Gemini 3.5 Flash: more expensive, but Google plan to use it for everything
description: Google released Gemini 3.5 Flash at Google I/O, skipping the preview modifier and going straight to general availability. Google appears to be using it for many key products. Simon discusses pricing and implications.
author: Simon Willison

title: The last six months in LLMs in five minutes
description: Simon's annotated slides from his five minute lightning talk at PyCon US 2026, covering major developments in LLMs over the previous six months.
author: Simon Willison

title: GDS weighs in on the NHS's decision to retreat from Open Source
description: UK Government Digital Service published 'AI, open code and vulnerability risk in the public sector' recommending to keep open by default. Making everything private adds delivery and policy costs, and can reduce reuse and scrutiny. Terence Eden interprets this as a major escalation in the disagreement over NHS closing repos in response to Project Glasswing vulnerabilities.
author: Simon Willison
